Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 670 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight from Buenos Aires to the city of Las Palmas in Argentina. On March 4, 1989, the flight encountered an accident during its approach to José María Sáez Airport in Las Palmas. This incident involved a Boeing 737-200 aircraft.

The aircraft experienced a loss of control and crashed shortly before landing, resulting in the tragic loss of all 25 people on board, including passengers and crew. The investigation into the crash revealed various factors, including issues related to pilot error and adverse weather conditions that contributed to the severity of the incident.

The tragic outcome emphasized the need for improvements in flight safety protocols and training for pilots, especially in handling adverse conditions during approach and landing.

While this incident was significant, Aerolíneas Argentinas has since worked to improve its safety record and continue providing air travel services throughout Argentina and beyond.
